# Ledge

> Ledge is a free, open-source (MIT) macOS app that turns the notch into a Shelf: a place to keep files, text and links for a moment, then drag them out wherever they need to go. It also shows live activities, like the Dynamic Island on iPhone. About 1 MB, written in Swift with the island drawn in the WebKit that ships with macOS.

- Shelf: drag files, folders, text or links toward the notch to drop them in; drag them out to any app, or copy with ⌘C and paste with ⌘V. Hover to peek, or press ⌃⌥S. Space opens Quick Look. Files are kept by reference and never copied, moved or changed.
- Live activities: while Apple Music or Spotify plays, the island shows the album artwork and bars that follow the music (macOS 14.2+ asks once for System Audio Recording; nothing is recorded or saved), with play, pause and skip on hover.
- Other apps can show a build, upload or timer with progress by opening a ledge://activity URL or posting the com.techreignera.ledge.activity distributed notification. No SDK.
- Macs without a notch (external displays, Mac mini): the island is a pill in the middle of the menu bar.
- Privacy: no account, no analytics. Its only network request downloads the album artwork of the song Spotify is playing.
- Requirements: macOS 13 Ventura or later, Apple silicon or Intel. One universal .pkg or .zip. Not signed with a paid Apple certificate, so macOS asks for confirmation once on first open.
